There's only one Jedi Operator in Star Wars Zero Company, and reckless players may end up with none at all: 'Be careful that nothing unfortunate happens to her!'
summary: Pad your wan.
body: Jedi are a key ingredient in most Star Wars adventures, but a little bit of a Jedi also goes a long way. Put too many Jedi in your Star War and you end up with an Attack of the Clones or a post-New Game Enhancements Star Wars: Galaxies —the magic and mysticism of those berobed space wizards drowned in a sea of lightsabers. With its upcoming tactics game Star Wars Zero Company , developer Bit Reactor appears to understand this well. According to a recent AMA hosted by the studio, there will only be one Jedi Operator in the entire game. What's more, if you act cavalier with them, you may end up with none whatsoever. As Bit Reactor has noted previously, permadeath is a major feature of Zero Company, with the main players in your adventure able to shuffle off this mortal coil at any point. For most classes, you will be able to recruit other Operators to fill in those class roles. But in the era when Zero Company is set, Jedi are supposed to be exceedingly rare. So what does this mean for Zero Company's Jedi Padawan operator, Tel-Rea? Can players recruit other Jedi operators if she dies? title: Hell Let Loose: Vietnam is open to all this weekend for a free playtest
summary: The 50v50 military shooter is gearing up for its full release in August.
body: If you're looking for something to do this weekend and would prefer it comes in the form of shooting guys, then allow me to direct your attention to Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, which is holding an open beta that's set to run until Monday. Announced in 2025 , Hell Let Loose: Vietnam is a more-modern follow-up to the WW2 milsim Hell Let Loose. It features the 50v50 battles of the original, expanded with the addition of air power—helicopters, naturally—across six large-scale maps. Battlefield Vietnam may be the obvious point of comparison, but as PC Gamer gunner Morgan Park pointed out, Hell Let Loose is more of a hardcore milsim. The Steam page reflects that as well, emphasizing the need for teamwork and tactics, and the game's focus on historical accuracy. To get in on that action, just pop around to the Hell Let Loose: Vietnam on Steam and punch the "join the playtest" button. The playtest is fully cross-platform, so you can jump in on consoles if you like—instructions for that are also available on Steam, but the short version is to look for the playtest on either the Xbox or PlayStation Store, and then install it. Console-exclusive servers are also being offered, for those who don'…

title: Even Japan's patent officials seem exhausted with Nintendo's antics as they refuse its 'absurd' defense of a rejected Pokémon patent
summary: Not a good sign when official patent office communications hit you with a snarky clapback.
body: While Nintendo has a long and infamous history of petty litigiousness, its recent efforts to secure a series of Pokémon-related patents have been particularly obnoxious —obnoxious enough that even the Japan Patent Office seems like its patience for the publisher's quibbling is wearing thin. Earlier this month, Japanese patent examiners issued a rebuke of Nintendo's objections to a Patent Office's prior rejections of one of the publisher's Pokémon patent applications. In its refusal of the publisher's arguments, the JPO's examiner was so atypically blunt that Japanese patent attorney Kiyoshi Kurihara described the exchange as containing "things rarely seen in standard patent practice" (via Automaton ). (Image credit: The Pokémon Company) At the heart of this particular squabble is Nintendo's Patent Application 2026-019762 , one of a number of patent applications the company has submitted in an attempt to secure ownership over systems related to Pokémon catching, battling, and riding. title: Saudi Arabia's takeover of EA gets approval from European Commission
summary: The commission has ruled that the buyout will not cause "competition concerns."
body: Saudi Arabia's proposed $55 billion acquisition of Electronic Arts has cleared one potentially significant hurdle, as the European Commission says it will not oppose the buyout. "The European Commission has approved, under the EU Merger Regulation, the acquisition of sole control of Electronic Arts Inc. of the US by the Public Investment Fund ('PIF') of Saudi Arabia," the ruling states (via RPS ). "The Commission concluded that the notified transaction would not raise competition concerns, given its limited impact on competition in the markets where the companies are active. The notified transaction was examined under the normal merger review procedure." The European Commission's approval of this deal came much more easily than its thumbs-up of Microsoft's acquisition of Activision Blizzard a few years ago, which spawned an in-depth investigation and specific commitments from Microsoft before the green light was given. But the EA deal is also quite a bit different: Not a merger, but a transfer of ownership that will see the company taken private. That carries significant risks of its own, including the $20 billion in debt EA will take on to finance the deal, but those factors don'…

title: Amazon Gaming boss says high hardware prices could be good news for its Luna cloud gaming program
summary: In a world of $1,000 Steam Machines, a hardware-free gaming option might have wider appeal.
body: The RAMpocalypse , and more specifically the obscene price inflation it's driven, sucks for just about everyone with an interest in gaming. But one person it maybe doesn't suck for is Amazon Gaming boss Jeffrey Gattis, who said in a recent interview with The Game Business that high hardware prices could be good for Luna, the company's cloud gaming business. Gattis said cloud gaming has historically "been a little bit of a solution in search of a problem," thanks primarily to the relatively low cost of consoles. Because of that, Amazon's goal with Luna hasn't been to supplant consoles, but rather to expand gaming to players who for one reason or another aren't interested in buying the requisite hardware. Given the way prices have gone (and will likely continue to go ), Gattis thinks, probably not incorrectly, that demographic is probably going to grow—and therein lies the opportunity. "We saw the Steam Machine opening at $1,000," Gattis said. "We hear rumors about consoles, because of the RAM crisis, pushing up over $1,000 in Gen 10. So, I do think you get to a point at which more people will be in the consideration set for a cloud gaming solution, just because of the sheer cost of…

title: Asus ROG Azoth Extreme Edition 20 review
summary: The type of keyboard you buy because you can, and boy does it shine.
body: After you spend above a certain amount of money on your gaming keyboard, you're not really paying for quality, specs, or competitive edge anymore. I felt this recently while testing out Melgeek's Centauri 80 . In my approximation, any more than $200 and you move into bragging rights/centrepiece territory, and by that logic, I reckon the Asus ROG Azoth Extreme Edition 20 is worth about three centrepieces. It's an expensive old beast, and $100 more than the already very pricey Asus ROG Azoth Extreme , which we reviewed back in 2024. But it's hard to say that Asus hasn't thrown absolutely everything at this new keyboard to celebrate the 20-year anniversary of ROG; you're getting an 8,000 Hz polling, up to 1,600 hours of battery life, a carbon-fibre positioning plate, as well as multi-layer dampening, plus a whole host of extra accessories and extras in the box. Oh, and did I mention the 24K-gold-plated commemorative nameplate? I probably should have mentioned the 24K-gold-plated commemorative nameplate. The Azoth Extreme is a very well-built bit of tech. It's super hefty, but it's heavy for a reason. It's sturdy, and though I wouldn't much like to drop a $600 gaming keyboard, I feel …

title: I suck at fighting games, but Marvel Tōkon has the sauce
summary: It could be the game that makes me a fan of the genre.
body: I will openly admit that I'm not usually a fighting game person . I enjoy playing Mortal Kombat with my equally bad friends, but as soon as I'm up against someone who knows their shit, I'm fumbling over the controls. Unsurprisingly, it's not all too fun getting your ass whooped and feeling like there's little you can do to stop the pain. But as soon as I laid eyes on Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls during Sony's 2025 State of Play, I knew I needed to at least try it—just look at the graphic design work on display. And now that the Marvel Tōkon beta has arrived, I've done just that. Marvel Tōkon's main selling point for a fighting game flump like me—besides the cool cast and art style—is the universal controls and automated combos. Basically, every superhero shares the same combo inputs, unlike, say, Mortal Kombat, where each character has unique chains. It's all standardised. Arc System Works Arc System Works Light, medium, and heavy attacks while standing, crouched, or aerial will always perform the same actions and automatically lead to specific chains no matter who you're playing. title: Minecraft Java Edition system requirements want 8/16 GB RAM for the first time, but it isn't more demanding now, Microsoft just hadn't updated the specs in a while
summary: The requirements are still light, but I remember what I was rockin' at launch.
body: Minecraft has been out a whole 17 years now, which makes me feel very old as I played it as a teenager when it launched, using (I believe) an AMD Phenom II X4 955 Black Edition and 9600 GT . Oh how times have changed. Now, Microsoft has updated its system requirements to 16 GB of RAM and an RTX 2060 or equivalent GPU for recommended performance in the Java version of the game. Comparing this to an archived snapshot of the requirements from May last year , that's 4x the RAM that was previously recommended, although another snapshot strangely does suggest that Microsoft recommended 4/8 GB back in 2022. title: The fourth biggest memory manufacturer could break into America soon, and chances are you've never heard of it
summary: DRAM-ing up support.
body: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) is planning to break into the US memory market. According to sources close to the matter, branching out overseas is part of a longer-term plan for the Chinese firm that has swiftly become the fourth-biggest maker of memory in the world. CXMT has been on my radar lately as multiple motherboard and PC component makers have made moves to validate its memory for their products . Considering the news that CXMT is reportedly massively ramping up its DRAM capacity during these times of memory shortage, it's not hard to see why. However, we're still a ways off from seeing CXMT DRAM become more readily available in the US; in the nearer term, CXMT will have to navigate both intense domestic demand in China, as well as Western competitor Micron urging US lawmakers to curb the company's access to key equipment , plus a sword of Damocles in the form of a spot on the Commerce Department's trade blacklist (via Reuters ). Not even Apple has been safe from the effects of the memory crisis , and has been keen to seek assurances CXMT won't be placed on the US' "Entity List ". summary: Well, that clears that up.
body: Bethesda is eager to reassure you that its house is not, in fact, on fire in the wake of 3,200 layoffs (1,600 that already happened, 1,600 that are still to come) at Xbox that claimed numerous devs at the studio, including the artist responsible for designing The Elder Scrolls' khajiit and argonians . Thus, its recent announcement that it currently has Fallout 3 and New Vegas remasters in the oven as well as an incoming, Obsidian-made Fallout. Now, in response to questions from YouTuber MrMattyPlays , Bethesda has said that the layoffs also won't affect its plans for The Elder Scrolls 6 . "The roadmap [for TES6] is unaffected," said the studio. That's all you're getting. No, really. Bethesda was ever-so-slightly more chatty about its plans for Oblivion Remastered. Yes, Bethesda has plans for Oblivion Remastered. I'm as surprised as you are. Since a one-two punch of patches the game got shortly after it released last year, the UE5-ified re-do of one of the funniest games ever made seems to have been largely forgotten , despite still having its fair share of performance hitches and bugs. Why are fans—who were sufficiently John-117-pilled to pay the advance access premium—underwhelmed? Oh, the classic reasons: bugs, server problems, utterly extraneous account linking requirements. title: Is Intel back? Company's latest earnings report remarkably different in tone to 12 months ago
summary: "I'm confident that Intel is well positioned to help define the next era of computing," says CEO Tan.
body: From leading technology company to talk of it being sold off to the highest bidder, Intel has had a bumpy ride as of late. The company just reported its Q2 2026 earnings, however, and they're surprisingly upbeat. Revenue, margins, and earnings per share are all above expectations, and even the Foundry business doesn't appear to be floundering quite so badly as it was once made out to be. Let's start with Foundry, Intel's manufacturing arm. When Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan joined the company a year ago, he threatened to halt development of cutting-edge process nodes (if not a death sentence, pretty close to one) if a big customer wasn't found or goals left unmet for the 14A process. "There are no more blank checks," Tan said at the time. Yet he couldn't sound much more positive about the Foundry business today. "My confidence in our foundry process roadmap has grown significantly since joining over a year ago. I am more confident than ever of the strategic in significant and unique value proposition of Intel Foundry," Tan says in the earnings call (via Seeking Alpha ). body: OtherSide Entertainment's stealth game Thick As Thieves launched in May of this year, but felt like it should have been in early access . Which was a problem, because the other game OtherSide was working on was cancelled, and now it's had two rounds of layoffs leaving fewer than 10 employees remaining. summary: The crowd is going nuts, they want their Dee Bradley Baker, they're chanting Matt Lanter's name: "Lan-ter, Lan-ter, Lan-ter!"
body: Ahead of a showing at Comic-Con in San Diego, StarWars.com has revealed the main cast of Star Wars Zero Company, the squad tactics game by ex-Firaxis XCOM vets. The topline for big Star Wars freaks: Dee Bradley Baker and Matt Lanter will be reprising their long-running roles as clone troopers and Anakin Skywalker respectively. (Image credit: Disney) Baker always reminded me of the actors in Elder Scrolls games (like the inimitable Wes Johnson ) in the way he elevated the high-volume job of voicing every clone trooper for like, a decade . It's something you could see becoming rote or workmanlike, but across multiple shows (most notably Dave Filoni's The Clone Wars), Baker put some zip into named clones and one-line mooks alike. His main role in Zero Company will be Trick, one of the game's RPG-like story companions. Lanter similarly defined Anakin Skywalker in the animated Filoni-verse. When I got to try Zero Company hands-on back in February, I clocked Baker as Trick immediately. The Summer Game Fest reveal that Anakin Skywalker will appear in Zero Company had me wondering if the Chosen One would get a similar treatment. title: A new expansion and the ability to be a crow wizard has me enjoying a 10-year-old action RPG for the first time
summary: Grim Dawn's Fangs of Asterkarn expansion pulled me in despite its old age.
body: I'm not even that far into my first ever playthrough of Grim Dawn and I can already see why I've heard people praise this game for the last 10 years. It's old, sure, but it's a surprisingly tight action RPG that despite its age hasn't been left to rust. The developers at Crate Entertainment have kept Grim Dawn from feeling like an action RPG that came out a decade ago. The quality-of-life additions in its final expansion, Fangs of Asterkarn , do a lot of the heavy-lifting, but even visually the game doesn't look that far removed from an older World of Warcraft zone. I've been playing quite a lot of Path of Exile 2 lately and was a little scared that Grim Dawn would be far too archaic for me. I think a major reason that hasn't been the case is that Fangs of Asterkarn gave it full WASD movement support, a control scheme I have a hard time letting go of in these types of games. It works so flawlessly in Grim Dawn that I would've assumed it was there from the start if I hadn't read the patch notes. title: Ubisoft chief says Sony's decision to kill game discs isn't going to be a big deal
summary: Yves Guillemot reckons the lack of physical discs might even be a good thing.
body: Sony's decision to stop producing game discs in 2028 has caused a real uproar. Some PlayStation owners see a dire future as they become dependent on digital services and lose the ability to trade old games in for new ones, while at least one analyst says we'll all get used to it quickly enough anyway. Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot has now weighed into the debate, and he's clearly in the "no big deal" camp. Guillemot was asked during today's quarterly investors call if Sony's decision might create "a demand headwind," because of the loss of the secondary market for PlayStation games. "What we saw on the PC is that it helped to grow the market," Guillemot said, presumably a reference to the explosive growth of Steam that drove a stake through the heart of physical PC game releases. "There's also some pressure for the future on the cost of machines, and being able to be only digital will help to have more accessible machines, I would say. There are pluses and minuses, but we think it will not disturb the industry too much." The impact of Steam on the evolution of PC gaming is obvious and undeniable, and while you might argue that it's not entirely a good thing (I certainly would), PC ga…

title: Crisol studio lays off all employees less than 6 months after launch, warns that full closure is a 'feasible possibility'

body: Less than six months after the release of the survival horror shooter Crisol: Theater of Idols , developer Vermila Studios appears to be in trouble. The studio has not officially closed, as one former employee had claimed, but CEO David Carrasco confirmed that employees have been let go and that a full shutdown "is a feasible possibility." Vermila's reported closure was initially shared on X by game designer Raúl Pernía Alejandro, who said (via auto-translation) that "Vermila Studios has initiated a redundancy procedure that has ultimately led to the studio's closure and the departure of the entire team." Several hours after that message was posted, however, it was deleted and replaced with one stating that while the "entire team" has left, "for now the company remains active." Alejandro acknowledged the mistake in a subsequent apology. (Image credit: Rauwuu_ (Twitter)) Still, it was clear that layoffs had taken place, as numerous employees on X and LinkedIn, some of them in senior positions and with long tenures and Vermila, reported that they'd been let go on July 22. title: Google slapped with $1 billion fine for violating EU's antitrust legislation
summary: Continued non-compliance could result in further penalties of 'up to 5% of [Google's] total worldwide turnover'.
body: The European Commission announced today it will fine a total of Google €890 million—or about $1 billion—for two violations of the EU's Digital Markets Act. The Search giant has 60 days to either address the violations or risk further penalty payments of "up to 5% of its total worldwide turnover" in the future. The Commission explained it is fining Google for "self-preferencing its own services on Google Search, and for putting in place restrictions on businesses to direct consumers to alternative, often cheaper, purchase channels on Google Play (steering)." These two violations have resulted in a fine of €460 million and a fine of €430 million respectively. Google has already begun work to redress these DMA violations by beginning to test "changes to how it presents its own services on Google Search for free services such as shopping, hotels and flights." The company will also review how it "presents shopping ads and content related services, such as sports." Google will apparently also make similar adjustments to AI Overviews and AI Mode. The European Commission says it will "continue its dialogue with Google," and "monitor the implementation of these solutions which constitute s…

title: Amazon walks back comments about taking 007 off of IO, but does say 'anything's possible' when it comes to buying the studio outright
summary: Not quite what I wanted to hear.
body: Amazon really confounded us all last month when, following the successful launch of 007 First Light, Amazon Gaming general manager Jeff Gattis mused that sequels would be "done by MGM and, theoretically, by Amazon Game Studios." Given that so many people—barring one uncontroversial and universally beloved PC Gamer writer—rather liked IOI's Bond game, it was incomprehensible to suggest yanking it away from the studio. Well, I guess Amazon itself has realised what a boneheaded move that would be, because in a recent chat with GI.biz , Gattis clarified that—insofar as the developer of the next 007 game is concerned—nothing is set in stone. "We did not confirm anything about who's publishing or developing the next Bond sequel… we haven't even discussed it really yet. The game's awesome. That's great. I think it's realistic to think that there would be a sequel." Then he states the obvious: "Given the success of this one, I think you probably want IOI developing it." Taken in tandem with an earlier comment, that "Technically, Amazon does own the rights to the game, but we're going to do what's right by the game, we're not trying to bring everything into Amazon," it does at least sound …

title: Early '90s animation tools were so primitive that Doom's lead artist says he pretty much did the whole thing with 'the undo key'
summary: The UnDoom key, if you will.
body: Human ingenuity is a powerful—sometimes terrifying—thing. Throughout history, no matter how basic the tools available to us, we have always found a way to build the weird obsessions that appear in our minds. You know, like Stonehenge, or the Pyramids, or Doom (1993). No, really. In a recent chat with Jesse Petrilla on YouTube , id co-founder and Doom lead artist Adrian Carmack revealed that, when it came time to put together the classic FPS' animations, the incredibly complex and advanced animation tool he used to do it was… the undo key. "As an artist, oftentimes you end up making your own tools," said Carmack. "You know, there was no animation tool, so I started using the undo key to create animation—the undo key in Deluxe Paint, so I'd go back and forth." If you're unclear as to how that works, remember that animations in original Doom weren't really animations as we think of them today, with models seamlessly transitioning through countless subtle movements to create smooth motion. Doom sprites, from your enemies to your weapons, were all very frame-y indeed. title: Lick your way to victory with the Mouth Pad, a Bluetooth device that lets you control your PC with just your tongue
summary: An early prototype looked like 'a lollipop with a bunch of sensors.'
body: PC gaming isn't always the most inclusive space. Besides the high price of everything from components to games, standard gaming peripherals such as a keyboard and mouse can exclude lots of folks with limited mobility. An expanding array of assistive devices is attempting to bridge that gap. Augmental describes itself as a company specialising in 'Skinware,' "body-coupled interfaces that let people control computers, communicate, and interact with AI without relying on their hands." Its latest project is the Mouth Pad, a custom-fit mouthpiece that allows users to control PCs, tablets, and phones with just their tongue. The device is now available to purchase in the US and, yes, you can absolutely game with it. The Mouth Pad looks like the top half of a retainer, with flexible circuits encased inside custom 3D printed dental resin. Mouth-based physical interfaces are nothing new in the assistive tech space , and mouth-operated pens are already used by gamers with physical disabilities. Rather than bashing your teeth against a physical joystick, Mouth Pad users can instead either run their tongue over the trackpad covering the roof of their mouth, or engage a head tracking mode in or…

title: Star Wars Zero Company is a 30-40 hour linear game with no New Game+, and I'm totally OK with this
summary: I'll actually be able to finish it. Hurray!
body: As someone who frequently finds themselves embroiled in gargantuan, branching RPGs and spends far too much time in live service romps, I really appreciate a game I don't need to dedicate my life to—a nice palate cleanser that's one and done. And it looks like Star Wars Zero Company falls into that category. In a recent Discord Q&A , developer Bit Reactor tackled the subject of game length, and while I certainly wouldn't call it short, it does sound pretty manageable. "Depending on your difficulty level and experience with the strategy genre, we estimate about 30-40 hours for the average player to complete the main story campaign," said lead producer Caydence Funk. We also know it's going to be a linear deal , with no branching paths or romances between operatives. So there are not a whole lot of reasons to dive back in once you've already concluded your Clone Wars misadventure. There's no New Game+ mode, either, though Funk notes that "players will unlock certain customisation options on subsequent playthroughs".
